title: Autonomous batcher: traffic quarantine and rollback window
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an autonomous batcher synthesis system that can propose batching and KV-prefetch configurations, apply them safely to a small fraction of traffic (traffic quarantine), monitor latency/throughput SLOs and automatically expand or rollback within a defined rollback window. The system should minimize per-token cost while ensuring P99 latency and throughput SLOs are never violated for production traffic.

Scope:
- Synthesizer: component that generates candidate batch/cache configs from workload traces and model profiles.
- Quarantine routing: route a small percentage (alpha) of production requests to the candidate config behind a traffic quarantine tag.
- Safety controller: limiters (per-route concurrent gates, token-rate caps), SLO-aware routing decisions, and anomaly detectors that trigger immediate rollback.
- Orchestration: safe apply path with staged expansion (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) and an automatic rollback window (config TTL and rollback triggers).

Non-goals: automated quantization changes (handled in separate flow), model architecture changes, or making permanent changes without human sign-off for high-impact routes.

Success metrics:
- Net per-token cost reduction on target routes >= 12% without exceeding SLO targets.
- False-positive rollbacks < 5% of candidate trials.
- Mean time to rollback on anomaly detection < 60s.

Design constraints and trade-offs:
- Aggressive batching improves cost but increases tail latency; safety controller must bias towards latency preservation for high-importance routes.
- Quarantine fraction should be computed per-route based on traffic variance and customer tier. Low-volume routes use longer quarantine windows.
- Avoid overfitting synthesizer to short-term spikes; use rolling 24–72h traces.

High-level flow:
1) Synthesis job produces candidate config with expected cost and simulated SLO impact.
2) CI-like validation runs in staging with synthetic load (best-effort).
3) Apply to production quarantine (alpha% traffic) via routing policy.
4) Safety controller enforces limiters and collects telemetry (latency quantiles, error rate, throughput).
5) If metrics stay within thresholds for the window, staged expansion occurs. Otherwise, automated rollback and alerting.

Telemetry and observability needs: detailed token-level latency histograms, per-quarantine cohort dashboards, rollout traces, and sample request logs (redacted). Feature flags and audit trail for config applies and rollbacks.

Integration points: routing service, runtime kernel selection, KV cache layer, console rollout UI, and Optimize recommendations service.

Deliverables: design doc, synthesizer prototype, safety controller implementation, routing integration, dashboards, unit/e2e tests, runbook and post-mortem template.
acceptance_criteria: Synthesizer can create candidate batching+prefetch config and persist it to the config store
Routing layer can apply a config to an isolated quarantine cohort and route alpha traffic
Safety controller enforces per-cohort concurrent and token-rate limiters and can signal immediate rollback
Automated staged expansion policy implemented with configurable thresholds and timers
Dashboard shows quarantine cohort metrics and exposes a one-click manual rollback
End-to-end experiment yields >=12% token-cost reduction on at least two representative routes without SLO violations
comments: 2025-10-21 - Planning: Reviewed proposal with PM (Ravi Kumar) and infra lead (Sofia Morales). Agreed to target high-volume public-cluster routes first. Action: Asha to draft design doc; Liam to prototype a minimal quarantine router patch.

2025-10-28 - Design review: Design doc v0.2 posted. Feedback from Product: quarantine fraction should be dynamic and tied to route SLA tiers. Feedback from Observability: need cohort-level P99 breaks and synthetic canary generators.

2025-10-30 - Decision: Use a conservatively low alpha (1%) for initial rollout; quarantine TTL 30 minutes by default for high-volume routes, 2 hours for low-volume routes. Limiters: (concurrent_requests_per_cohort, tokens_per_minute_per_cohort).

2025-11-01 - Implementation: Synthesizer prototype completed (Python pipeline). Simulated runs on last-7d traces show expected cost reductions 10–18% depending on route patterns. Edge case: bursty routes show spike in tail latency when batch-window > 50ms.

2025-11-02 - Safety controller: Implemented anomaly detector using EWMA + z-score on P99. Worked during local tests - triggered rollback on synthetic spike. Need to tune sensitivity to reduce false positives.
notes: Risk: If anomaly detector thresholds are too loose we may under-react and violate SLOs; if too strict we may rollback useful optimizations — calibration required.
Follow-ups: tie quarantine expansion to customer tier and billing alerts; add manual 'force-accept' flow for experiments with business justification.
Next steps: 1) complete limiter primitives in runtime (ENG-68211 follow-up), 2) finish router patch and run alpha on staging, 3) schedule canary in production for 2025-11-10 window.
